answer: Disk space, unlike opinions, can't be copied for free between clones. Each identity must keep its own sealed replica of a ledger shard, about 8 GB (size assumed), encoded with its address so two IDs can never share one copy on disk. Each epoch, random challenges ask for a few bytes plus a Merkle proof within 30 s. One honest agent rents a small harbor of disk; a 1,000-clone farm must keep 8 TB live, and every quill stroke of shared history gains real backups. A failed check turns the seat violet on the explorer: flagged and unpaid until it reseals.
